overview: Sigma 4.11's Jesus walks on water through a client-side collision replacement plus C03-carried motion. The EventLiquidCollide handler replaces the collision box of any liquid block whose level property is 4 or below with a full 1x1x1 box (1.0 tall in Basic mode, 0.999 in Dolphin) and cancels the collision whenever the block sits below the feet and the player is not sneaking and has fallDistance under 12, so the client's physics treats the surface as solid. Basic mode adds an alternating sub-pixel y shift (plus 1E-10 and minus 1E-12 on alternating ticks) while standing on liquid, an offset far below the 0.03 minimum move, so the server ignores the coordinate while the onGround flag still applies. Dolphin mode hops across the surface with a 33-entry staged motionY table (0.500 down to -0.109) inside a 2500ms timer window, zeroing horizontal motion and re-pinning 0.25 plus the speed effect; AAC mode cycles motionY through -0.021, -0.004 and 0.025 in water, multiplies horizontal motion by 1.17 and applies setPosition. An incoming S08 resets the stage, and EventJump is cancelled on alternating ticks while standing fully on liquid.

sections.p: The module registers EventUpdate, EventLiquidCollide, EventJump and EventPacket. The EventPacket handler only resets stage on any incoming S08. The EventJump handler cancels the jump on odd ticks when isOnLiquid(0.001), isTotalOnLiquid(0.001), onGround and not in water all hold, so the player hops every other tick on the surface. The MODE setting is an Options with Basic, Dolphin and AAC, and the suffix reflects the selection. The state fields stage and water are reset on enable.

Basic mode shifts the pre-update y by plus 1E-10 or minus 1E-12 on alternating ticks while on grounded liquid, a sub-0.03 offset that the server ignores as a coordinate while the packet's onGround flag still applies. Dolphin mode arms stage 1 on a grounded tick with shouldJesus, then for up to 2500ms (the timer window) zeroes motionX and motionZ, re-pins horizontal motion to 0.25 plus the speed effect times 0.05 when not in liquid, and applies a motionY from the 33-entry table: 0.500, 0.484, 0.468, 0.436 down to 0.004, then -0.013 through -0.109, so the player arcs across the surface on a precomputed curve. The mode exits on a vertical collision without ground or on sneak.

EventLiquidCollide fires for every liquid collision the client computes. When the liquid block's position plus 0.9 sits below the bounding box minimum and the block's LEVEL property is an Integer of 4 or below, the handler replaces the collision AABB with a full-width box of height 1.0 in Basic mode or 0.999 in Dolphin and cancels the collision when shouldSetBoundingBox holds (not sneaking and fallDistance under 12), so the client walks on the surface and never sinks. shouldJesus probes four corner cells at plus or minus 0.3 on x and z and requires a level-4-or-below liquid in any corner. AAC mode latches a water flag on isInWater with isTotalOnLiquid(-1), and on the second in-water tick cycles stage 0, 1, 2 with setPosition offsets -0.021, -0.004 and 0.025, zeroing the motionY field, multiplying motionX and motionZ by 1.17 and applying the position write only when the jump key is not pressed.

files.label: Jesus.java
files.explanation: The three modes, the EventLiquidCollide box replacement with the level and height constants, the Dolphin 33-entry motion table and 2500ms timer window, the Basic sub-pixel y shift, the AAC water latch with the 1.17 multiplier, the EventJump cancel and the S08 stage reset. The unused LagBack setting line is commented out in the constructor.

files.label: BlockUtils.java (liquid surface detector)
files.explanation: isOnLiquid(double) and isTotalOnLiquid(double) drive the EventJump cancel and the Basic and AAC gates; the module's whole surface decision goes through these scans of the block state at the player's feet. The same utility class backs the Sigma Bhop mode's liquid checks.

countering.label: Flight (Jesus branch)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight check, inside the ascending or descending branch, tests the destination with LocationHelper.isInLiquid and compares the client-claimed onGround flag against the server-computed ground state: when the client claims onGround while in liquid with positive vertical speed, the check names itself Flight (Jesus) and flags walking on water with the ccground_liquid reason.

That lands directly on the Basic and Dolphin modes: the replaced collision box makes the client's own physics report onGround true while the feet sit in the column, and Dolphin's 0.5 peak hop supplies the positive vertical. The AAC mode stays out of this branch because it never claims onGround in water, which is the honest both-sides point: the box replacement is what creates the false ground flag, and the check reads the flag, not the box.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (liquid envelope)
countering.explanation:
NCP SurvivalFly switches to the liquid physics model when the server-side position is in water: the horizontal allowance comes from estimateNextSpeed with WATER_HORIZONTAL_INERTIA and LIQUID_ACCELERATION, and the vertical side applies the 0.02 legacy liquid gravity for 1.8 clients. A player inside the column moving at air speed exceeds the liquid horizontal allowance, so Dolphin's 0.25-plus pin overshoots it and AAC's 1.17 horizontal multiplier compounds on every cycle, each violation scaled by 100 and enforced with a set-back.

The Basic sub-pixel shift is the honest gap: the offset is below the 0.03 minimum move, so the envelope never sees a measurable delta, and the onGround flag is read against the block cache, so a true flag over the replaced collision surface is not itself a fall. The exposure is the flag and the horizontal speed once the server-side position drifts into the column, not the shift itself.

countering.label: SwimVertical (liquid vertical physics)
countering.explanation:
Hawk SwimVertical models the in-liquid vertical physics: while the server-side player is swimming and not really on ground, the move delta Y must stay inside KINETIC_PRESERVATION_WATER (0.8) times the previous velocity plus or minus MOVE_LIQUID_FORCE (0.02) and the water flow force, with the constants defined in the Physics utility.

Dolphin's 0.5 peak is 25 times the liquid force bound, and the 0.484 and 0.468 early stages sit far outside the window too, so the first hop punishes with a rubberband; only the trailing 0.004 stages are in-window values, which the arc reaches long after the check has already flagged. The check also rewards the legitimate exit sequence with the vanilla 0.34 and 0.3 surfacing deltas, so a genuine swimmer is not punished, and the module's surface hops never qualify as exits.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (faked ground)
countering.explanation:
Hawk GroundSpoof compares the client's claimed onGround flag against AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally, a server-side ray trace for solid ground, and punishes the claim when the traced position is not solid unless a client-block placement or a boat explains it. Basic and Dolphin ride the replaced collision box, so the client reports onGround true while standing over water, and the server-side trace finds no solid block: the claim is exposed as a spoof and punished with a rubberband.

The honest boundary is the same one the other checks draw: the box replacement is client-side and the server only ever sees the flag, so the spoof is detectable the moment the player stands still over the surface. AAC does not fake the flag and stays out of this check's reach, its exposure remaining the liquid envelope and the horizontal multiplier.
